mainTopic: Moving leftover נסכים to another זבח (לב בית דין מתנה), and which animals connected to a תודה need loaves
overview: The גמרא first explains that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows his father רבי שמעון: blood that is ready to be sprinkled counts as already sprinkled. It then asks how the משנה can let נסכים set aside for one זבח go with a different זבח. רבי ינאי answers that בית דין silently makes a condition on them (לב בית דין מתנה). That condition cannot apply to oil, which is part of the מנחה itself. It also cannot release the נסכים to חולין, because of a גזירה about כלי שרת. Following מתתיה בן יהודה, the נסכים may go only to a זבח slaughtered at that very moment. If there is none, they are immediately treated as disqualified by לינה. The גמרא shows that רבי שמעון does accept the court's silent condition, and his ruling on unneeded תמידין is different because those animals can graze until they get a blemish. A new משנה then teaches that the offspring, replacement and תמורה of a תודה are offered without loaves, and a ברייתא brings the sources in the פסוקים. Finally, רבי יוחנן limits this rule to after כפרה, and רב עמרם asks which case רבי יוחנן means. He shows that the replacement case would teach nothing new; the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר follows his father: ready-to-sprinkle counts as sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון follows his father's rule that blood standing to be sprinkled is treated as already sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון holds like his father, who said: anything that is standing ready to be sprinkled is treated as if it was already sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's opinion from the earlier discussion: he follows his father רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that once blood is in the cup and ready for זריקה, it is treated as if the זריקה already happened. So even if the blood spilled before it was sprinkled, the offering counts as complete, and that is why the נסכים can still be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: Whatever is ready to be sprinkled is treated as already sprinkled
Sprinkling the blood of a קרבן on the מזבח
He holds like his opinion

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
holds like his father,
who said: anything that stands to be sprinkled
is considered as sprinkled.
phrases.notes: He means the blood, already in the cup and ready for the מזבח, even if it spilled before being sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָותֵיהּ דַּאֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's opinion from the preceding discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood that is ready to be sprinkled is treated as already sprinkled (רבי שמעון), and רבי אלעזר follows this.

steps.title: How can נסכים go to another offering if oil cannot go to another מנחה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that נסכים may go with another זבח, and challenges this from רב חסדא's rule about oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if there is another זבח, the נסכים should be brought with it. But רב חסדא said: oil set aside for this מנחה is not allowed to be used for a different מנחה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה, then immediately attacks it with a ruling of רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא teaches that something set aside for one specific offering is locked to that offering. If that is true for oil and a מנחה, it should also be true for נסכים and their זבח, so how can the משנה switch them to a different זבח?

keyTerms.meaning: Wine (and flour-oil) offerings that come along with a זבח
A different animal offering
He set it aside (designated it)
Flour offering
But isn't it so that (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: The Master said:
If there is another offering,
they should be offered with it.
phrases.notes: "They" are the נסכים that were made holy for a זבח that became פסול.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chisda say:
Oil that one set aside for the sake of this meal offering
is unfit for the sake of another meal offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the משנה's rule about moving נסכים to another זבח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that נסכים may be brought with another זבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא says something designated for one offering cannot go to another; the same should apply to נסכים.

steps.title: בית דין silently makes a condition on the נסכים
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי answers that בית דין silently stipulates that unused נסכים will go to another זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: בית דין has in mind a condition on them: if they are needed, they are needed; and if not, they should be for another זבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי answers the challenge by saying the נסכים were made holy with a built-in condition from בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נסכים are not locked to one זבח, because בית דין always intends: use them for this זבח if it works out, and if not, use them for another. Because of this unspoken condition, switching them is allowed, unlike the oil in רב חסדא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: The court silently makes a condition (in its mind)
They were needed
A condition

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
The heart of the court stipulates concerning them:
phrases.notes: Literally "the heart of the court," meaning בית דין has this condition in mind without saying it.

phrases.english: if they were needed, they were needed,
and if not, they should be for another offering.

steps.whatToRemember: לב בית דין מתנה: בית דין silently conditions the נסכים, so they can move to another זבח.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: לֵב בֵּית דִּין מַתְנֶה עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב חסדא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a hidden condition that makes the case different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נסכים are locked to their original זבח just like oil to its מנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית דין's silent condition lets unused נסכים go to another זבח.

steps.title: Then why not the same condition for oil?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בית דין's silent condition doesn't apply to oil as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the oil too should have this condition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי ינאי's answer: if בית דין makes a condition on נסכים, why not on oil for a מנחה too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a silent condition is enough to free the נסכים, the same idea could free the oil, and then רב חסדא's rule would make no sense. So the גמרא asks what makes oil different.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Also, too

phrases.english: If so, the oil as well?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי ינאי's answer by extending it to oil.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's answer of לב בית דין מתנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the condition works for נסכים, it should work for oil, which would contradict רב חסדא.

steps.title: Oil is part of the מנחה itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that oil is part of the body of the מנחה, unlike נסכים which only accompany the זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Oil is part of the מנחה itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the condition can't work for oil: the oil is part of the מנחה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נסכים are a separate item that comes along with a זבח, so they can be conditioned to go with a different one. Oil is mixed into the מנחה and is part of it, so it belongs to that specific מנחה and cannot be switched.

keyTerms.meaning: The body (an actual part) of the מנחה

phrases.english: Oil is the body of the meal offering itself.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think נסכים are part of the זבח the way oil is part of the מנחה. נסכים only accompany the זבח; that is exactly why they can switch.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the condition doesn't extend to oil.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Oil and נסכים are the same, so both should get the condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Oil is part of the מנחה, while נסכים only accompany the זבח.

steps.title: Why not condition the נסכים to become ordinary?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בית דין doesn't make a condition that unused נסכים simply become חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let בית דין make a condition on them that they go out to be חולין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: if בית דין can make conditions, why not make the condition that unused נסכים become ordinary, not holy at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a silent condition is possible, a simpler one would be to release the נסכים completely to חולין when the זבח is פסול. The גמרא wants to know why בית דין chose only to switch them to another זבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them make a condition
Ordinary, non-holy things

phrases.english: But let them stipulate concerning them
that they go out to non-sacred status?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי ינאי's condition and asks why it isn't broader.
steps.kashyaTarget: The limits of בית דין's silent condition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בית דין can condition the נסכים, it could condition them to become חולין.

steps.title: A גזירה so people won't think holy things can become ordinary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חכמים forbade this condition so people wouldn't think one may take things out of כלי שרת to חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a גזירה, so people won't say: one may take things out of כלי שרת to become ordinary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית דין doesn't make that condition because of a rabbinic גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the נסכים are made holy in a כלי שרת, people who see them become ordinary would not know about any hidden condition. They might wrongly think holy things can just be taken out of the כלי שרת for regular use. To prevent that mistake, the condition only allows switching to another זבח.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic protective decree
Lest people say
Service vessels of the בית המקדש, which make things holy

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest they say:
We may take out from service vessels to non-sacred use.

steps.whatToRemember: נסכים can move to another זבח because of לב בית דין מתנה, but they cannot become חולין because of a גזירה about כלי שרת.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the condition doesn't release the נסכים to חולין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית דין could simply condition the נסכים to become חולין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים prevented this so people won't think holy items can leave כלי שרת for ordinary use.

steps.title: Shouldn't there also be a decree against moving נסכים to another offering?
steps.stepSummary: Using the same worry from step 7, the גמרא argues that moving נסכים to a different זבח should also be forbidden, so people won't think נסכים set aside for one offering may be used for another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now too, let there be a decree, lest people say: libations that someone set aside for this offering are fit for a different offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the reasoning of step 7 back against רבי ינאי's answer. If the חכמים worry about people drawing wrong conclusions, they should worry here too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, the חכמים banned a condition that would make נסכים become חולין, because people might draw a wrong lesson. The same logic seems to apply to moving נסכים to another זבח, since people might think נסכים are not tied to the offering they were set aside for. So the condition of בית דין from step 3 looks like it should be banned too.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake or a wrong practice
Libations: wine (and the accompanying flour and oil) brought with a זבח
That he set them aside (designated them)
A different animal offering

phrases.english: Now too, let there be a decree
phrases.notes: "Now too" points back to step 7, where the חכמים made a decree so people wouldn't learn the wrong lesson.

phrases.english: lest people say:
Libations that one set aside for the sake of this offering
are fit for the sake of a different offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning of step 7's answer to challenge רבי ינאי's condition from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The silent condition of בית דין that unused נסכים go to another זבח (step 3).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a wrong public impression is enough reason to ban one condition (חולין), it should be enough to ban the other condition (another זבח), since people may think נסכים can be freely switched.

steps.title: מתתיה בן יהודה: only when another offering is being slaughtered right then
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a teaching of מתתיה בן יהודה: the משנה's case is when another זבח happened to be slaughtered at that very moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But מתתיה בן יהודה taught: for example, where there was an offering slaughtered at that very time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The נסכים are moved only to a זבח that is being slaughtered right then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the other זבח is slaughtered at the same moment, an onlooker just assumes the נסכים were meant for it from the start. So nobody learns the wrong lesson that נסכים can be switched between offerings, and no גזירה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering that has been slaughtered
At that very time, at the same moment

phrases.english: But Mattitya ben Yehuda taught:
for example, where there was an offering slaughtered
at that very time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by limiting the משנה to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה refers only to when another זבח is slaughtered at the same moment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The נסכים could be moved to any later זבח, which would invite a mistaken impression.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are moved only to a זבח slaughtered right then, so onlookers see nothing strange and no גזירה is needed.

steps.title: Why didn't the משנה state this distinction directly?
steps.stepSummary: If the rule depends on whether a זבח is slaughtered right then, the משנה should have said so openly instead of ending with "if not, they are disqualified by לינה."
steps.simpleTranslation: But if there is no offering slaughtered at that time, what happens? They become disqualified by being left overnight? Then rather than teaching in the end clause, 'If not, they are disqualified by being left overnight,' let the משנה make the distinction within the case itself: 'When is this said? Where an offering was slaughtered at that time; but if no offering was slaughtered at that time, no.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges מתתיה בן יהודה's answer from the wording of the משנה. If his limit is right, the משנה should have stated it clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to מתתיה בן יהודה, when no זבח is ready right then, the נסכים would just sit and become invalid overnight. But the משנה's סיפא seems to describe a different case, where there is no other זבח at all. The גמרא asks: if the real dividing line is "slaughtered at that moment or not," why didn't the משנה say so directly with "when is this said"?

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes invalid by being left overnight
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Rather than teaching
Let it make the distinction and teach it within the same case
"When is this said?": the standard way to limit a rule to a certain case

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין זֶבַח זָבוּחַ בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה, מַאי?
phrases.english: But if there is no offering slaughtered at that time, what?
It becomes disqualified by being left overnight?
Rather than teaching in the end clause:
If not, they become disqualified by being left overnight,
let it distinguish and teach within the case itself:
In what case is this said?
Where there was an offering slaughtered at that time,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין זֶבַח זָבוּחַ בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה – לֹא.
phrases.english: but if there is no offering slaughtered at that time, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּתָנֵי סֵיפָא: אִם לָאו יִפָּסְלוּ בְּלִינָה, לִיפְלוֹג וְלִיתְנֵי בְּדִידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit set in step 9 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: מתתיה בן יהודה's limit of the משנה to a זבח slaughtered at that very time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule depends on timing, the משנה's ending ("if not, disqualified by לינה") is a roundabout way to say it. The משנה should have stated the timing distinction directly.

steps.title: That is exactly what the משנה means: without a ready offering, they are invalid at once
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the סיפא does mean this: if no זבח is slaughtered right then, the נסכים are immediately treated as if they had already become invalid by לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is indeed what it is saying: When is this said? Where there was an offering slaughtered at that time. But if no offering was slaughtered at that time, it is treated as though they were disqualified by being left overnight, and they are disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's ending already teaches the distinction. "If not" means "if no זבח is slaughtered right then."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "they are disqualified by לינה" does not mean we wait until morning. It means that once no זבח is ready at that moment, the נסכים immediately count as if they were left overnight, and they are invalid. This keeps מתתיה בן יהודה's limit in place and fits the משנה's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: "That is indeed what it is saying": reading the existing text the way the challenger wanted
It is treated as if they were already disqualified
Invalid, unfit for the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: Leftover נסכים may go only to a זבח slaughtered at that very moment (מתתיה בן יהודה). If none is ready right then, they are immediately treated as if they were left overnight, and they are invalid.
steps.confusionAlert: "Disqualified by לינה" here does not mean we actually wait overnight. The נסכים are invalid right away, as if the night had already passed.

phrases.english: That is indeed what it is saying:
In what case is this said?
Where there was an offering slaughtered at that time,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין זֶבַח זָבוּחַ בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה –
phrases.english: but if there is no offering slaughtered at that time,
it is treated as though they were disqualified by being left overnight, and they are disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי קָא אָמַר: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by reading the משנה's סיפא as already containing the requested distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה's wording: the סיפא is itself the "when is this said" distinction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Disqualified by לינה" refers to a separate case where the נסכים actually wait overnight.
steps.terutzMaskana: If no זבח is slaughtered at that moment, the נסכים are immediately treated as disqualified by לינה.

steps.title: Does רבי שמעון really accept the court's silent stipulation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its earlier explanation from a teaching of רבי יוחנן. There, רבי שמעון forbids redeeming unneeded תמידין while they are unblemished, so it seems he does not accept לב בית דין מתנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי שמעון בן אלעזר really hold that the court silently makes a condition about them? Didn't רבי יוחנן teach about daily offerings that the public ended up not needing: according to רבי שמעון they may not be redeemed while unblemished, but according to the חכמים they may be redeemed while unblemished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own explanation of the משנה. It brings a teaching showing that רבי שמעון seems to reject the idea that the court silently makes a condition on offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא let the נסכים go to another זבח because the court silently stipulates this when they are set aside. But in the case of unneeded תמידין, the חכמים let them be redeemed unblemished, which only works if the court made a condition, while רבי שמעון does not. So it looks like רבי שמעון does not accept לב בית דין מתנה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The court silently makes a condition in its mind about how sacred items will be used
The daily communal offerings brought every morning and afternoon
Are redeemed, meaning their holiness is moved onto money
Unblemished, still fit to be brought on the מזבח
The public, the whole community

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: But does Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar hold
phrases.notes: The point is the view of רבי שמעון, which his son follows. The next lines quote רבי שמעון directly.

phrases.english: that the court silently makes a condition about them?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Idi bar Avin say

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
phrases.english: that Rav Amram said that Rabbi Yitzchak said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Daily offerings that the public did not end up needing:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֵין נִפְדִּין תְּמִימִים,
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Shimon, they are not redeemed while unblemished;
according to the Rabbis, they are redeemed even while unblemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר לֵב בֵּית דִּין מַתְנֶה עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basis of the explanation built up in the earlier steps, that the court's silent stipulation allows the נסכים to move to another זבח
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה, following רבי שמעון's school, relies on לב בית דין מתנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redeeming unblemished תמידין is allowed only through the court's condition. רבי שמעון forbids it, so he must reject לב בית דין מתנה.

steps.title: The daily offerings are different because they can graze
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון does accept the court's stipulation in general. The תמידין are different because they have another way out: they can graze until they get a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because they have a solution through grazing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The case of the תמידין is special, so it does not show that רבי שמעון rejects the court's stipulation in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court only needs to make a silent condition when there is no other way to avoid losing the sacred item. Leftover תמידין can be left to graze until they become blemished and are then redeemed, so no condition is needed. Leftover נסכים have no such solution, so even רבי שמעון agrees the court makes a condition for them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; the cited case is special
A fix or solution that avoids a loss
Grazing: leaving the animal in the pasture until it gets a blemish

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון does accept לב בית דין מתנה. He only skips it where there is another solution, like letting animals graze until they are blemished.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the leftover תמידין from the last step.

phrases.english: because they have a solution through grazing.
phrases.notes: An animal can be left in the pasture until it gets a blemish, and then it may be redeemed. נסכים have no such option.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאִית לְהוּ תַּקַּנְתָּא בִּרְעִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by limiting the תמידין case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's ruling on the תמידין shows he rejects the court's silent stipulation everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court makes a condition only when there is no other way to prevent a loss. The תמידין can graze, but the נסכים have no such way out, so for them even רבי שמעון accepts the stipulation.

steps.title: The offspring, replacement and substitute of a thanks offering need no loaves
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that the offspring of a תודה, its תמורה, and a replacement animal set aside when the original was lost are all brought without the לחם. A פסוק in ויקרא is the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The offspring of a thanks offering and its substitute, or a case where someone set aside a thanks offering, it got lost, and he set aside another in its place: these do not need loaves. This is because the פסוק says 'he shall bring with the thanks offering.' The thanks offering itself needs loaves, but its offspring, its replacement and its substitute do not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three animals connected to a תודה that are brought as offerings but without the usual loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal תודה must be brought with forty loaves. The משנה reads 'הַתּוֹדָה' in the פסוק as meaning only the original thanks offering. Animals that get their holiness from it are offered, but without the loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: The offspring of a consecrated animal
A substitute: an animal someone tried to swap for a consecrated one, which becomes holy too
A replacement animal set aside after the original was lost
The loaves that must come with a תודה
A thanks offering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up תמורה and חילוף. A תמורה is an illegal swap that makes a second animal holy. A חילוף is a proper replacement for a lost animal; here the original was later found.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new topic: which offerings connected to a תודה carry the requirement of the לחם.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The offspring of a thanks offering, and its substitute;
or if one set aside a thanks offering and it was lost
and he set aside another in its place,
phrases.notes: The first animal was later found, so the second one is the extra animal being discussed.

phrases.english: it does not require loaves,
as it is stated: 'Then he shall bring with the thanks offering' (ויקרא 7:12):
the thanks offering requires loaves,
but neither its offspring nor its replacement
nor its substitute requires loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the original תודה requires the לחם. Its offspring, its replacement and its תמורה are brought without loaves, based on 'הַתּוֹדָה' in ויקרא 7:12.

steps.title: The verse lets him bring either animal with its loaves
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches from the words "התודה יקריב" that if a lost תודה was replaced and then found, the owner may bring whichever animal he wants, along with its loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: What does the פסוק "if he sacrifices it for a thanks offering" come to teach? Suppose someone set aside his תודה, it got lost, he set aside another in its place, and then the first one was found, so now both are standing. How do we know he may bring whichever one he wants, with its loaves? The פסוק says "the thanks offering he shall sacrifice."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to find the source in the פסוקים for the משנה's ruling. It starts with a case where the owner has two possible תודה animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of "the תודה" in general, not one specific animal. So whichever of the two animals he chooses counts as his תודה. The one he picks comes with the loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: A thanks offering, which is normally brought together with forty loaves
Someone who sets aside an animal for a specific קרבן
"The verse teaches": introduces the פסוק that proves the point
"From where do we know?": asks for a source

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
What does it teach when it says "he sacrifices a thanks offering"?
"If he sacrifices it for a thanks offering":
From where do we know, regarding one who set aside his thanks offering and it was lost,
and he set aside another in its place,
and then the first one was found,
and now both of them are standing,
from where do we know that whichever of them he wants
he may sacrifice, with its loaves along with it?
The verse says: "The thanks offering he shall sacrifice."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה quoted in step 14 by bringing the פסוק-based source.
steps.raayaObject: Either of the two animals may be offered as the תודה, with its loaves.

steps.title: Only one animal gets loaves
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from "יקריבנו" ("he sacrifices it") that only one of the two animals needs loaves, not both.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the second animal also needs loaves. So the פסוק says "he sacrifices it": one, not two.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It rules out the idea that the second animal also needs loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "יקריבנו" is singular: "it." So only one animal brings the loaves. The second animal is still offered, but it comes without לחם.

keyTerms.meaning: "You might have thought": brings up a possible mistaken idea
Needs loaves to be brought with it
"He shall sacrifice it": singular, meaning only one

phrases.english: You might think the second one also needs loaves?
The verse says: "He sacrifices it":
one, and not two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 15: both animals may be offered, but only one comes with loaves.
steps.raayaObject: The second animal does not need loaves.

steps.title: Offspring, replacements, and substitutes are offered without loaves
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from "אם על תודה" that offspring, replacements, and תמורות are offered. It learns from "על זבח התודה" that only the original תודה needs לחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק included the second animal for offering and excluded it from loaves. How do we know to also include offspring, replacements, and substitutes for offering? The פסוק says "if for a thanks offering." You might think they also need loaves. So the פסוק says "then he shall sacrifice with the thanks offering": the תודה itself needs loaves, but not its offspring, its replacement, or its substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by extending the rule to the three animals from the משנה: offspring, replacement, and תמורה. They are all offered, but none of them brings loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate questions here, and each gets its own פסוק. Are these animals offered at all? Yes, from "אם על תודה." Do they need loaves? No, from "זבח התודה," which points only to the real תודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק included one thing and excluded another
The offspring born to a קרבן animal
A replacement animal set aside after the original was lost
An animal someone tried to swap for a קרבן, which then becomes holy too

steps.whatToRemember: Offspring, replacements, and תמורות of a תודה are offered as קרבנות, but only the original תודה brings לחם.

phrases.english: Since the verse included and excluded,
phrases.notes: He means the second animal: it was included for offering but left out of the loaves.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת וְלָדוֹת וַחֲלִיפוֹת וּתְמוּרוֹת לְהַקְרָבָה?
phrases.english: from where do we include offspring, replacements, and substitutes for offering?
The verse says: "If for a thanks offering."
You might think they also need loaves?
The verse says: "Then he shall sacrifice with the thanks offering":
the thanks offering needs loaves,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא וְלָדָהּ וְלֹא חִילּוּפָהּ וְלֹא תְּמוּרָתָהּ טְעוּנִין לֶחֶם.
phrases.english: but not its offspring, nor its replacement, nor its substitute need loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same pattern (offered, but no loaves) to the three animals listed in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that offspring, replacements, and תמורות are brought without לחם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: "אם על תודה" and "והקריב על זבח התודה".

steps.title: The rule applies only after atonement
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא sends in the name of רבי יוחנן that these animals go without loaves only after the owner got his כפרה. Before כפרה, they do need loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא sent a message in the name of רבי יוחנן: The משנה taught this only after atonement. But before atonement, they need loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement limits the משנה's rule. רבי יוחנן says the "no loaves" rule applies only once the owner has already brought his תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After כפרה, the owner's obligation is already done, so an extra animal is just a leftover and brings no loaves. Before כפרה, that animal may itself be the one that fulfills his obligation, so it needs loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Atonement; here, the point when the owner has fulfilled his obligation by offering the תודה
"They taught this only": limits a rule to a certain case
He sent a message (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי יוחנן as arguing with the משנה. He is narrowing it: the "no loaves" rule is only for after כפרה.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח רַב חֲנִינָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥanina sent in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
They taught this only after atonement,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's rule that offspring, replacements, and substitutes come without loaves.

phrases.english: but before atonement, they need loaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח רַב חֲנִינָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source of the משנה to a limit on how far it applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offspring, replacements, and תמורות of a תודה go without loaves only after כפרה. Before כפרה, they need loaves.

steps.title: Which case is meant?
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם asks which case in the משנה רבי יוחנן's limit refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם discussed it: To which case does this refer?
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם asks a clarifying question about רבי יוחנן's statement. This sets up the next step, where he tries one possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three kinds of animals: offspring, replacement, and תמורה. רב עמרם wants to know which of them רבי יוחנן's "before or after כפרה" rule is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: He discussed it (looked into it closely)
"To which one?": asks what case is being referred to

phrases.english: Rav Amram discussed it: To which case does it refer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the scope of רבי יוחנן's statement from step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the משנה's cases רבי יוחנן's limit applies to.

steps.title: If it means the replacement of an obligatory thanks offering, nothing is new
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם tries reading רבי יוחנן as talking about the replacement of an obligatory תודה. He shows that both halves of the rule were already taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it refers to the replacement of an obligatory תודה: if it means before atonement, we already learned it! If it means after atonement, we already learned it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם tests the first possible answer to his own question and attacks it. On that reading, רבי יוחנן's statement teaches nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before כפרה, the ברייתא already said he may bring whichever animal he wants, with its loaves. After כפרה, the ברייתא already said only one animal gets loaves. So reading רבי יוחנן as talking about the replacement adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you say": brings up a possible reading in order to test it
A תודה the person was obligated to bring, such as one he vowed

phrases.english: If you say it refers to the replacement of an obligatory thanks offering,
if before atonement, we already learned it!
phrases.notes: In step 15: he may bring whichever one he wants, with its loaves.

phrases.english: if after atonement, we already learned it!
phrases.notes: In step 16: only one animal gets loaves, not two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the first answer to step 19's question and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רבי יוחנן's statement as being about the replacement of an obligatory תודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On this reading, both the "before כפרה" and "after כפרה" halves are already taught in the ברייתא, so רבי יוחנן's statement would add nothing.
